sections.h2: Where is Shelby County, Kentucky, and which towns does it include?
sections.html:
Shelby County lies between Louisville and Frankfort and belongs to the Louisville metropolitan area. The legislature created it in 1792 from land that had been part of Jefferson County, and it carries the name of Isaac Shelby, Kentucky's first governor. Shelbyville is the county seat. The other incorporated cities are Simpsonville and Pleasureville, and Pleasureville sits partly in Henry County.

The county covers 386 square miles, with 380 of them land. Its high point is Jeptha Knob at 1,188 feet, and Guist Creek Lake offers 325 acres of fishing water. Henry, Franklin, Anderson, Spencer, Jefferson and Oldham counties touch its borders. Interstate 64, U.S. 60 and U.S. 421 and state routes 53 and 55 carry most traffic, and Shelbyville itself sits on U.S. 60 about two miles north of the interstate, which was built in 1960.

Smaller places such as Bagdad, Finchville, Christianburg and Clay Village are unincorporated and fall under county government alone. Shelbyville calls itself the Saddlebred Capital of the World.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Shelby County homes and incomes?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists 51,243 residents for July 2025, up from a base of 48,113 in April 2020, and 20,391 housing units. The county is mostly owner territory, which shapes both the tax roll and the typical sale.

  • Share of homes lived in by their owners, 2020 to 2024: 73.9 percent.
  • Median value of those homes: $304,800.
  • Monthly cost of ownership: $1,636 with a mortgage and $549 without.
  • Median rent: $1,033, across 18,484 households of about 2.58 people.
  • Median household income: $82,604, with 9.9 percent of residents in poverty.

These are among the higher figures you will find in Kentucky counties of this size, and they reflect the pull of nearby Louisville and the county's industrial parks west of Shelbyville.

sections.h2: How does the Shelby County PVA assess real estate?
sections.html:
The Property Valuation Administrator is a state office with county jurisdiction. Every parcel is valued at 100 percent of fair cash value, meaning the price a willing buyer and willing seller would agree on, as of January 1. The PVA does not set rates or take payments. Your bill combines that assessed value with rates adopted by state, county and city governments, school boards and special districts.

Ownership for tax purposes is also frozen on January 1. A parcel bought after that date still produces a bill in the former owner's name until the next year, although the PVA tries to mail it to the new owner using the recorded deed. New owners who receive nothing should call the Sheriff. The PVA can be reached at 502-633-4403.

sections.h2: When are Shelby County property tax bills due, and what do late payments cost?
sections.html:
Kentucky's statewide schedule applies (KRS 134.015). Paying in full on or before November 1 takes 2 percent off. From November 2 through December 31 the printed amount is due without penalty. A payment in January carries 5 percent, and one after January 31 carries 10 percent.

The Sheriff collects the bills. The county's own notice says that after April 15 penalties are added and interest keeps accruing, because unpaid claims are then filed with the County Clerk, who keeps the delinquent tax records. A statutory collection fee is added to delinquent bills (KRS 134.119). The Sheriff's website has a Current Tax Bill Lookup, and the office number is 502-633-4324.

sections.h2: How can a Shelby County owner appeal an assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the PVA. State law keeps the real property tax roll open to the public for 13 days beginning on the first Monday in May, with six days of access each week including Saturday, and a taxpayer who wants to appeal must first ask for a conference during that period (KRS 133.045). The 2026 period has ended, and the next opens in early May.

Bring evidence. Recent sales of similar houses nearby, a fresh appraisal or repair estimates carry weight, and a request without paperwork rarely moves the number. If the conference leaves you unsatisfied, the published notice explains how to file with the local board of assessment appeals, and the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals hears cases from there.

sections.h2: Which tax breaks can Shelby County homeowners claim?
sections.html: All property is taxable unless the Kentucky Constitution exempts it, and the main relief for homeowners is the homestead exemption for older owners and the disability exemption. A formal application must be filed with the PVA before an exemption can be granted. Ask that office for the current exemption amount and age rule, because the dollar figure is adjusted over time.

sections.h2: How should property tax be handled when a Shelby County house sells?
sections.html:
Closing agents usually prorate the year's tax between buyer and seller, and the title company pays off any unpaid balance from the sale proceeds. Ask the Sheriff for a bill lookup before you sign a contract so you know whether last year's bill is still open. The County Clerk records the deed and collects the seller's transfer tax of 50 cents per $500 of price (KRS 142.050). A deed at the county's typical $304,800 value owes $305.00, with partial $500 blocks rounded up.

sections.h2: What are the choices for selling a Shelby County house with tax owed?
sections.html: You can pay the balance from the proceeds of a listing, sell on your own with the same payoff at closing, or take a cash offer that is already adjusted for what is owed. Each route needs a current payoff figure from the Sheriff, and a house with delinquent bills may need that cleared before a conventional lender will close.

faqs.q: When are Shelby County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payment in full on or before November 1 earns a 2 percent discount, and the printed amount is due through December 31. A 5 percent penalty applies in January and 10 percent after January 31. The county reports that penalties and interest build after April 15.

faqs.q: Who sends the tax bill when a Shelby County house sells mid-year?
faqs.a: The bill stays in the name of whoever owned the property on January 1. A buyer who gets nothing should call the Sheriff at 502-633-4324 or use the online bill lookup.

faqs.q: Where can I check a Shelby County tax bill?
faqs.a: Use the Current Tax Bill Lookup on the Sheriff's website, or call the Sheriff's Office. The office is at 501 Main Street in Shelbyville and keeps weekday hours from 8:30 to 4:30 except holidays.

faqs.q: How do I apply for the homestead exemption in Shelby County?
faqs.a: File a formal application with the Property Valuation Administrator. The county says no exemption can be granted without one. Call 502-633-4403 to learn the current age or disability requirements.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax does a Shelby County seller pay?
faqs.a: Fifty cents for each $500 of the price, rounded up by $500 block. A sale at $304,800 owes $305.00, and the County Clerk collects it when the deed is recorded.
